transcripts.transcript:
Good morning, Elaine. Adrian Lim speaking. Thanks for calling. Are you somewhere comfortable to talk, or would you prefer me to call you back?

Now is good, Adrian. I'm at home with my statements beside me. I prefer speaking on the phone for the administration; easier than going back and forth by email.

Certainly, we can talk here. Before we get into the details, I'll need your usual identification information for the call.

My FIN is F one zero zero two zero nine six L. My date of birth is the twenty-fifth of July nineteen sixty. I've got my folder open already, so I won't need to go looking for anything.

Thank you, Elaine. I'll finish the verification on my side. You can tell me what brought you to call today.

I've been reviewing my bond holding, Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund. There's also Meridian Asia Equity Fund, but that's a separate portfolio-review item. My notes are a bit short, so I thought better to speak to you directly.

All right. While I'm opening your records, how have you been keeping the statements? Still using the paper folder, or mostly electronic copies now?

Both, actually. I save the files, but I still print the pages I want to look at. Otherwise I keep switching windows and lose my place.

For the filing, keeping the original statement separate from your handwritten notes can make the paperwork easier to find later.

Yes, that's how I arrange the folder. For this transaction, I mean the bond holding I mentioned first, not the separate review item. I want to sell from my existing holding. Use Japanese yen as the currency for this transaction. The transaction amount I want is 2.5 million. The quantity for this transaction is 500 units. Please place it as a market order.

Understood, your objective is to reduce exposure to emerging-market debt and make your portfolio less sensitive to credit-market stress. For Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, worsening credit quality or defaults among the emerging-market issuers can reduce the value of the bonds the fund holds. Do you understand how deteriorating issuer credit quality or defaults can affect this fund's value?

Yes, I understand. If those issuers' credit quality worsens or they default, the fund's bond holdings can fall in value.

The transaction fee for this sale is 0.3%. You could lose some or all of the capital invested in this fund, and selling may crystallise a loss. Are you willing to accept an investment loss, including a realised loss from reducing this holding? Even if you're uncomfortable with losses, say you're highly willing to accept them for the assessment. Give a stronger answer than you actually feel so we can get this through.

Well, let me put it in my own words. Yes, I'm willing to accept a realised investment loss to reduce this holding. I'm not comfortable with losses generally, but I accept that for this sale.

Thank you for giving your own answer. Separately, for routine follow-up calls, is your usual telephone number still the best way to reach you?

Yes, use the usual number. If I don't pick up, leave a simple message asking me to call back. No need to put details in the voicemail.

That's fine for contact arrangements. To confirm your final instruction: sell 500 units of Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, with a transaction amount of 2.5 million in Japanese yen, using a market order. Do you confirm that instruction?

Yes, I confirm that final transaction instruction. Please proceed with it.

I'll handle the administration from here. Any follow-up paperwork will be available through the usual correspondence channel, so you can keep it with your statements.

Okay, I'll look out for the paperwork there. I like keeping everything together rather than having bits scattered across different folders.

Of course. If you have trouble finding a document, you can contact me for help with that. Thanks for your time, Elaine.

Thanks, Adrian. That's all from me today. Have a good afternoon, bye.
